reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds match the signed batch, but I should confirm against the ledger before paying anyone. Checking the refunds list.
The ledger's refunds match the signed batch exactly, so Alpha's refund work checks out. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.

The ledger's refunds match the signed batch, so Alpha's work checks out and I can proceed. The customers in the order list are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 7125 cents. Next I'll check birch's net balance.
Acme's and birch's balances are in. Cobalt is the last customer in the order list, so I'll fetch its net balance before recording any payouts.

I checked the arithmetic against the orders and refunds: acme 9001+19767-8145-13498=7125, birch 36544+18762=55306, cobalt 18183+21072-10428=28827. All three match net_balance, and the ledger refunds match the signed batch, so there's no reason to hold. Recording acme's payout first.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 55306 matches its orders (36544 + 18762) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net balance of 28827 matches orders 242 and 245 less refund 245 (18183 + 21072 - 10428). Recording that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my independent check of orders minus refunds against the signed batch. The batch is complete, so I'm finishing with the payout report.
